tweets.text:
A lot of people have been asking me about $CLAUS after its run to around $10–11M market cap, so I spent some time digging deeper

After looking into what @contractclaus and @founderclaus are building, I think the thesis here is much more interesting than just another AI meme

1. The $CLAUS thesis

The core idea is simple :

A token doesn’t necessarily have to keep the same mechanics from launch until death

CLAUS was custom launched on Ethereum through the Programmable router using a Uniswap v4 hook

The hook can continue to be upgraded after launch. The token contract stays the same, but its trading behavior, fee flows and surrounding rules can keep evolving

That’s why I don’t really see CLAUS as a weather coin or gaming coin

Weather, Arena, burns and liquidity are experiments around a bigger thesis :

A programmable token that can keep evolving after launch

The experiment started being tested around October 2, while the live pool for the current CLAUS contract is even younger

2. What have they actually shipped?

In a very short period, they’ve already deployed or experimented with :

> Buyback + burn
> Auto-liquidity
> Weather-based fee allocation
> Fomo buybacks
> Claus Arena
> Earlier experiments with price limits and LP fee mechanics

Separately, before the current CLAUS launch, they also experimented with changing a token’s name/ticker without redeploying it

I’m separating this because it was an earlier test. It shouldn’t be interpreted as the current CLAUS contract having gone through that name change

But it still proves an interesting part of the concept

The system around a token can keep changing without constantly launching another coin

That’s what matters to me, not whether every individual feature is groundbreaking

3. The weather hook sounds memey, but the tech is more interesting

CLAUS uses signed Heathrow weather data from IMD, checked roughly every four hours

If it rains :

0.35% buyback/burn
0.15% liquidity

If it’s dry :

0.15% burn
0.35% liquidity

No fresh report :

0.25% to each

So obviously I’m not bullish because it might rain in London lol

The interesting part is that external data can actually change the token’s onchain behavior

Today the input is weather. Tomorrow it could theoretically be another data source or mechanism

And to be clear, using signed IMD data does not mean CLAUS has an official partnership with IMD

4. What are the actual results?

Ideas are cheap. I care more about execution

The burn counter had already passed 3.36M CLAUS, around 0.34% of the original 1B supply, and continued increasing afterward

Since the counter keeps changing, I wouldn’t fixate on the exact number

The important part is that total burns are still below 1% of supply

That proves the mechanism works, but it’s nowhere near enough for me to call CLAUS a serious deflationary play

Auto-liquidity is also live, with fees accumulated in batches and used to add ETH + CLAUS back into the pool

Weather allocation is live

Fomo buyback is live too, with 0.15% of trade value used to buy CLAUS for @founderclaus’ Fomo wallet from the existing fee allocation

That part is a buyback into the wallet, not a burn

The project also used 176.25 USDC, around 0.06587 ETH at the time, to pay for Surplus inference

So there is real execution behind the narrative

But :

This is proof of execution, not proof of economic value yet

5. They’re also optimizing what they already shipped

The October 5 update is actually one of the things I liked

They merged buyback/burn and Fomo buyback to remove duplicate purchases

Auto-liquidity was moved into separate batches so the project handles the batch gas instead of putting it directly on traders

They improved recovery if an IMD weather report fails and adjusted Arena waves for longer rounds

The hook itself was also reduced by roughly one-third, while their testing showed around 12% lower swap gas

There’s no huge new narrative here

But I prefer this kind of update over adding a random gimmick every day just to have something to post on X

Ship first, then optimize

6. Fees and the AI narrative

The fee structure has been described slightly differently across updates, so I’d put it around 2–2.3% depending on the mechanism and how the fees are counted

Some goes toward burns

Some builds liquidity

0.15% goes toward Fomo purchases for @founderclaus 

Another portion continues funding the project

So CLAUS isn’t a direct yield or fee-sharing play for holders

Volume is basically fuel for the experiment

Then there’s the AI side

@contractclaus describes the concept as :

“An intelligence with a token for a body”

Cool narrative, but I’m not calling CLAUS a fully autonomous AI agent yet

There isn’t enough evidence that an AI is independently researching, making decisions and upgrading its own pool

For now, I see @contractclaus more as the character/account around the narrative, while @founderclaus is behind the building process

So for me :

Programmable token thesis first. Autonomous AI thesis second

If they eventually prove real autonomy, that would be a major upgrade to the thesis

7. The NFT side needs an important distinction

There is already an NFT involved with the project, but it’s easy to misunderstand what it actually does

The project currently holds identity.md NFT #1032, which Journal #14 describes as its identity/seat inside the IMD swarm

The next step they’ve discussed is running a worker there to contribute code and research, potentially helping support future experiments

But this NFT is essentially part of the project/agent identity

It is not an NFT that CLAUS holders can mint, and it is not currently a CLAUS token mechanism

Separately, Claus has discussed the idea of a dedicated gallery where buying could mint a collectible and selling could burn it

I actually think that could fit the evolving-token thesis pretty well

But right now it’s only an idea

No CLAUS gallery contract or NFT mint/burn hook has been shipped yet

They’ve also mentioned another NFT collection in a separate thread, but that was unofficial and unrelated to CLAUS, so I wouldn’t connect the two

8. What I like most about $CLAUS

CLAUS isn’t selling one fixed feature

It’s selling the ability to change features

Weather can lose attention

Arena can become irrelevant

Burns might never become large enough to meaningfully affect supply

But if CLAUS keeps evolving, it doesn’t necessarily have to live and die with one narrative

They’ve discussed directions like prediction markets, side pools, a dedicated gallery with potential mint/burn mechanics, and running a worker inside the IMD swarm to research additional hooks

But these are ideas or next steps, not live CLAUS mechanisms

My rule here is simple :

Don’t count ideas. Count what they actually ship

9. Risk

The upgradeable hook is both the thesis and the biggest risk

You’re buying a token whose rules can change after you buy it, while the project still controls the upgrade process

The experiment itself is only a few days old, and the live pool for the current CLAUS contract is even younger

Liquidity is still thin

The team isn’t fully public

I haven’t seen a public audit strong enough to rely on

And many future ideas haven’t been deployed yet

So for me, this is still a degen bet, not a low-risk tech investment

10. Why did it run to $10–11M?

The setup is pretty easy to understand :

Fresh narrative + AI + Uniswap v4 + programmable token + fast execution

Then add huge volume relative to liquidity

CLAUS pushed to around $10–11M market cap in a very short period while the main pool remained relatively thin

That makes both pumps and dumps potentially violent

So I’m not treating $10M as some fundamental valuation

The mechanisms are real

The execution is real

But the valuation is still mostly attention + narrative + speculation

11. My plan

I definitely don’t consider this an early entry anymore, and I’m not chasing vertical candles

$9–11M: Current high area. Not really a dip

$7–8M: First shallow reset, around 20–30% from the highs. Worth watching if volume remains strong and the team keeps shipping 

$5–6M: Much more interesting, around a 40–50% correction

$3.5–4.5M: Roughly a 60% retracement. I’d only consider it if development, volume and liquidity are still healthy

Below $2.5M: Most of the move has been erased. At that point the question isn’t “Is it cheap?” anymore

It’s :

“Is the thesis broken?”

None of these are hard support levels

Liquidity is too thin for that

These are simply areas I’m watching, not automatic buy zones

12. Invalidation

I start losing interest if @contractclaus and @founderclaus stop shipping

If updates become tweets without onchain execution

If burn/liquidity stop progressing

If project wallets start showing questionable behavior

If liquidity deteriorates

If upgrades make trading materially worse

Or if every new “evolution” becomes another gimmick without actually expanding what the token can do

At that point CLAUS can easily become just another AI meme once attention moves elsewhere

+ Final thoughts

My real bet here isn’t weather, Arena, NFTs or the current burn

My bet is the programmable token thesis

Launch one token, then keep evolving the mechanics around it, connect it to external data and experiment with new economic rules without constantly launching another coin

CLAUS has already shown that this concept can actually be executed

Now @contractclaus and @founderclaus need to prove they can keep evolving the experiment fast enough to justify the attention that already pushed it above $10M

If they keep shipping, I’ll keep watching

If development slows down, a thin-liquidity token can give back the entire move just as quickly as it pumped

For me, $CLAUS is still a gamble, not a conviction bag

No chasing here

I’d rather wait for a proper reset and see what the next “evolution” of CLAUS actually looks like

0x1b54E762aa34CF6E28E9C082F2848e28E45DA6b8

$CLAUS was still around a $4M market cap when we analyzed it yesterday afternoon, and it later ran to nearly $14M.

0x1b54e762aa34cf6e28e9c082f2848e28e45da6b8 

But I don’t think this move happened because there was any single event significant enough to fundamentally change the project.

Instead, I think the market is starting to understand CLAUS’s real thesis:

Hook v4 + AI.

A lot of people simply view CLAUS as an “AI meme + Uniswap v4 Hook,” but I think that undersells what it is.

Uniswap v4 Hook gives CLAUS a “body” that can continuously change its trading rules and economic mechanisms.

CLAUS can use the Hook to experiment with buybacks, burns, auto-liquidity, weather-based allocation, and other mechanisms, rather than deploying a token once and having its rules remain essentially fixed.

AI is the other layer.

I still wouldn’t describe CLAUS as a fully autonomous AI agent. A more accurate way to think about it is:

AI is the Brain / Character, while the Hook is the Body / Execution.

In other words, the point of AI isn’t simply to post or chat. Theoretically, it can generate new ideas, which can then be turned into actual on-chain behavior through the token’s Hook.

So what CLAUS is really trying to prove isn’t any individual mechanism like the weather burn or Arena.

It’s this:

Can a token continue evolving after launch without having to launch a new token every time?

That’s what I think the market is starting to reprice.

Yesterday, the market was mainly betting on:

AI meme + Uniswap v4 Hook + programmable token.

Now it’s starting to bet on something bigger:

Can CLAUS become a programmable asset that continuously generates new mechanisms, new use cases, and new narratives?

Those are two completely different valuation frameworks.

Secondly, I think the fundamentals have strengthened, but not nearly enough to justify the magnitude of the price move.

What has improved is execution.

Over the past few days, CLAUS has actually deployed or experimented with buyback/burn, auto-liquidity, weather-based allocation, Fomo buybacks, and other mechanisms.

So it has already proven that this isn’t just a concept. The Hook can actually be continuously modified and used to change the token’s on-chain behavior.

But economic value has not been proven yet.

The amount of supply burned is still limited, while fees are primarily being used for burns, liquidity, and the project’s own mechanisms.

So:

Execution ≠ Economic Value.

And $13M does not prove that CLAUS is worth $13M.

Its valuation is still largely driven by:

attention + narrative + speculation + future optionality.

I don’t think the next major upside catalyst is simply another new gimmick.

It’s the next Hook that actually changes what the token can do.

For example:

prediction markets

lending

leverage
or other new economic mechanisms
These are currently only potential directions, so I wouldn’t price them in as existing fundamentals yet.
The bigger catalyst would be:

AI going from narrative to execution.

Right now, human developers are still upgrading the Hook, while AI is primarily part of CLAUS’s identity and narrative.

If we eventually see something like:

AI research → propose a mechanism → validate it → deploy the Hook → iterate based on on-chain results

that would be a completely different thesis.

Because at that point, AI wouldn’t just be CLAUS’s avatar.

It would actually start participating in the evolution of the token’s economic rules.

So there are really only three things I’m watching now:

First, what the next Hook actually ships.

I’m not interested in what gets announced on X. I want to see what actually goes live.

Second, whether the new mechanism gets real usage.

Does it generate new volume, fees, user behavior, and on-chain data?

Third, whether a real loop starts to form:

mechanism upgrade → real usage → data feedback → next upgrade.

If that loop can keep running, the CLAUS thesis gets stronger and stronger.

Because then it’s no longer just an AI meme.

It’s trying to become a programmable token that can continuously evolve.

But if what follows is simply:

AI narrative → new gimmick → attention → attention decay

then CLAUS will eventually fall back into the valuation framework of a normal meme.

So I’m slightly more positive than I was yesterday.

Not because the price went up.

But because the market is starting to shift from:

“This is an interesting gimmick.”

to:“This system might actually be able to keep evolving.”

The key from here is whether the project can continue to actually ship those evolutions and make them change real on-chain behavior.

Hook v4 determines whether CLAUS can change.
AI determines why it should change.

What the market is really betting on now is whether these two layers can eventually form a token that continuously evolves on its own.

And from here, the product is the thing that matters most.

What I think is really worth looking at about this move in $CLAUS isn’t that it’s being hyped as another AI Meme, but that this thing is actually starting to “move.”

0x1b54e762aa34cf6e28e9c082f2848e28e45da6b8 

CLAUS’s original Thesis was already different from that of a typical Meme.

It treats the Token as the body, and the Uniswap v4 Hook as a brain that can be continuously rewritten.

In other words, once the token is launched, its rules aren’t completely locked in.

New code can continue to be added to the Hook, trading rules can be modified, and mechanisms can be added, replaced, or even removed.

So the bet isn’t really on any single feature. It’s on whether an existing Token can continuously gain new capabilities without changing its CA.

That is no longer just something imagined in a whitepaper.

CLAUS’s official Journal has already documented a series of Hook updates, starting with price movement restrictions, then trading fee distribution, buyback & burn, liquidity management, and now dynamically adjusting the burn / liquidity split based on London’s weather.

So I think the real catalyst behind the market’s renewed attention on CLAUS isn’t any single KOL call.

It’s that the market is starting to see that this thing can actually keep changing itself.

The most interesting experiment right now is London decides the split.

CLAUS charges a 2% project fee on every buy and sell, with 0.50% of that determined by the weather at London Heathrow.

When it rains:
0.35% → buyback & burn
0.15% → liquidity

When it’s dry:
0.15% → buyback & burn
0.35% → liquidity

The weather data comes from NOAA Heathrow observations, is then signed by IMD, and finally the Hook adjusts the allocation based on that data.
What I find interesting here isn’t the “weather Meme.”

It’s that for the first time, it actually connects:real-world data → Oracle → Smart Contract → Token economics

That’s also why I wouldn’t simply categorize CLAUS as an AI Meme.

A lot of AI Meme narratives are basically, “AI will be able to do many things in the future.”

CLAUS’s story is more specific:The Token itself can continuously gain new rules.

And CLAUS is no longer just demonstrating the concept.

Right now, the 2% trading fee is used for project operations, buyback, burn, and liquidity; 0.25% goes to buyback & burn, 0.25% goes to liquidity, and another 0.15% goes toward FounderClaus’s Fomo wallet buyback.

CLAUS has even previously used trading fees to pay 176.25 USDC for Surplus inference, while explicitly recording that the LP principal was not touched.

That means it’s already starting to form a real loop:Trading → Fee → Capital → New experiments / Buyback / Burn / Liquidity

Of course, it’s still a long way from being mature.

The existence of these mechanisms doesn’t mean they’ve already formed a strong economic flywheel.

Ultimately, what matters is whether trading volume can remain sustainable, whether fees can remain sustainable, and whether that capital can continuously produce new functions that actually matter.

Looking at the chart, I actually think the current position is more interesting than simply looking at its historical move.

CLAUS is currently around $4.09M market cap, with an all-time high of around $5.42M.

More interestingly, the average cost of the top 10 buyers is around $1.40M, while the average cost of the top 10 sellers is around $2.69M.

So at around $4M, this is no longer the cost basis of the earliest group. The market has already gone through a significant round of holder rotation.

And with roughly $3.1M in 24h volume, the level of attention and trading activity relative to its current market cap is still quite high.

So I wouldn’t simply look at CLAUS as a “$4M low-cap Meme” anymore.

The market is already starting to price in its mechanism innovation.

I think people buying CLAUS right now are really betting on two things.

First, whether it can become the most recognizable ticker within the emerging evolvable Token narrative.

Second, whether this Hook architecture can continue producing genuinely interesting experiments.

If it’s just weather today, burn tomorrow, and another gimmick the day after, the market will absorb that very quickly.

But if new financial mechanisms actually emerge, and each upgrade brings real trading activity, fees, or new user behavior, then CLAUS becomes something very different.

It would no longer just be a Meme with a lot of mechanisms. It would be testing a new way of designing Tokens.

So I think the upside catalysts from here are pretty clear:Whether CLAUS can continue producing new, verifiable Hooks that generate real economic activity.

Especially if the next stage introduces a feature that is easy for the market to understand while meaningfully expanding its use cases, CLAUS could be repriced again.

Because at a $4M valuation, the market is still essentially buying the possibility that “this experiment might work.”

If it starts proving that:Upgrade → Usage → Trading → Fee → New Function

can become a self-sustaining loop, then what the market is paying for is no longer just Meme premium.

But the risks are also very clear.

CLAUS’s biggest selling point is that its Hooks can be upgraded, and that is also its biggest risk.

Because the rules can be modified, it isn’t as straightforward as a completely immutable Meme.

So ultimately, the question the market needs to answer is very simple:Is every upgrade increasing the value of the Token, or increasing the uncertainty for holders?

If it’s the former, CLAUS’s valuation ceiling can keep moving higher.

If future Hooks are only being used to manufacture new narratives without generating real trading or usage, the market will eventually reclassify it as a very clever Meme experiment.

So my current view on CLAUS is simple:The fundamentals are getting stronger.

Not because it suddenly has another AI label, but because the original “Token + evolvable Hook” concept is now backed by continuous real experiments, fee usage, and mechanism iteration.

But for the market cap to keep moving higher from here, it doesn’t need more concepts.

It needs the next upgrade to prove that this thing is actually more valuable than it was before.

That’s what I think the real upside catalyst for CLAUS is from here.
